name: Courtside
reference: Nike campaign posters: a huge condensed headline over a subject, one hot colour, high contrast.
pattern: Black, white and one volt yellow-green.
personality: Momentum. A condensed headline slams over a subject; cuts whip on the beat.

motion.character: Fast pushes, whip transitions, hard cuts on the beat.
motion.transitions: A whip pan with motion blur in the direction of travel, or a hard cut.

grammar: One condensed headline per scene, as large as it fits.
The volt marks the one word or number that wins.
A real subject (photo or silhouette) sits behind the type.
needs: A photo or silhouette of the subject.

exceptions.reason: Volt on black is the sports-campaign reference itself, used on one word or number, never as a UI accent or a glow.

pictures.note: A real subject behind the type; the subject crosses the headline but every letter reads.

footage.note: Hard black and white b-roll: a net, a court, a shoe. Framed low under the end card.

music.feel: dark trap, heavy 808, determined, building to a drop

hits.note: A whoosh on a panel or a whip; an impact on the cut to the last card. The drop lands on the biggest change.

compose.how: The photo fills the frame with `over: true`; the words go behind the cut-out subject through placeBehind (cover.ts), so no word loses a letter. When the athlete fills the text-safe area and no place keeps every letter, the words take a band of the ground at the top and the athlete fills the frame under it; the picture starts under the words (lineInBand with overlap), so the head may rise in front of the words' foot only where placeBehind keeps every letter whole (a letter's foot carries its name). At 16:9 the band is a column beside the athlete. Keep the figure: never set the words across the body.

hook.how: The subject and the first condensed word on frame 0, with the bed audible under it (a kick, when the track has one there).

moves.move: A huge condensed headline over the subject; the subject breaks a word that still reads.

measurable.how: No letter more than 30 % covered; the word covers at least 60 % of the width.

moves.move: A whip pan with motion blur in the direction of travel.
The volt marks the one word or number that wins.

measurable.how: The accent covers one word per key frame.

moves.move: The drop lands on the biggest change.

measurable.how: The largest picture change sits within 2 frames of the drop.

props.over: true, with the words placed by placeBehind (cover.ts) so no word loses a letter behind the subject; when placeBehind finds no place (ok false), set the words in front: over false

blocks.for: The subject behind and over the type.
The condensed words, one cap height, cut on the kick.
The volt ground on the drop, behind the words (a colour that stays is a ground; a wipe crosses the frame and leaves).

props.moves: 6-frame pushes of 6-8 % on each word cut; pin the words (kineticWords `pinned: true`) so the push moves the picture, never the edge-to-edge type
props.whips: the whip to the end card, blurred along its travel

blocks.for: A whoosh on the whip, one impact on the cut to the end card.
The offer in display at full width, its when and where under it.

avoid.why: The offer is the loudest frame, not a small label.
A poster states, it does not plot.

ends.how: The offer at full width in the volt, its when and where under it, with the one impact on the cut.
ends.with: the offer as `name` at full width in the volt, `line` the when and where, the one impact from `hit` on the cut

mix.note: Dark trap. Enter so the drop lands on the biggest change.

shots.match: One athlete, one light; wide, mid and tight on the beats.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
